source_checks.requirement: Q3: How do local visibility and commercial readiness differ?
source_checks.evidence: 01 / THE FOUR-ZIP MARKET BRIEF Less territory. More useful detail. Four ZIP codes set the research boundary. Your service, your capacity, and your most pressing question set the direction. 01 See how you show up. Examine the local search journey, Google Business Profile information, service-area clarity, and what a potential customer can actually find. 02 Follow the inquiry. Trace the route from interest to contact. Look for unclear services, broken paths, missing information, and handoffs worth checking. 03 Choose the next move. Separate the observed finding from the assumption. Give the next action an owner, a review date, and the evidence needed to assess it. Local-search reference: Google’s published guidance ↗ Define your four-ZIP scope ↗ THE FOUR-ZIP MARKET BRIEF SAMPLE FORMAT A clear territory. A question worth answering. RESEARCH AREA ZIP 01 RESEARCH AREA ZIP 02 RESEARCH AREA ZIP 03 RESEARCH AREA ZIP 04 OBSERVATION What did we actually see? EVIDENCE Source, date, and context NEXT ACTION Who does what next, and why? Open the sample brief ↗ A SECOND PATH Get ready for commercial. Commercial readiness begins with your capabilities and a separately confirmed project need. Local visibility asks how customers discover and contact you; commercial qualification asks whether the work, authority, timing, and capacity fit. Read the qualification note ↗

source_checks.requirement: Q4: Where do the research inputs come from and how are they checked?
source_checks.evidence: A SIGNAL NEEDS A SOURCE Know what’s behind the next move. Our working method keeps the observation, its source, the date checked, and the unanswered questions together. Recommendations and illustrative examples are labeled separately from verified findings. 01 / LOCAL VISIBILITY Google Business Profile guidance Google’s published guidance describes relevance, distance, and prominence in local results. We use that guidance as a reference for profile accuracy and visibility research, without a ranking promise. Read Google’s guidance ↗ 02 / COMMERCIAL RESEARCH Official county benchmarking data Montgomery County’s public data is one research input. Our process requires separate confirmation of current authority, project intent, scope, and permission before describing a record as an opportunity. Explore the county dataset ↗ References checked October 29, 2026. Field notes and service descriptions are editorial drafts. Actual project facts require their own dated evidence.

source_checks.requirement: Q5: Does this preview provide live leads, guaranteed rankings, or verified projects?
source_checks.evidence: A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS Know what you’re starting with. What is the Four-ZIP Market Brief? + It is a focused review format for an HVAC business: four ZIP codes, one core service, and a question about visibility or the customer journey. A researched brief pairs observations with sources, unknowns, and one next action. The builder on this page prepares the scope and worksheet for that work. Who is MBRACE INSIGHT for? + HVAC owners and operators in Washington, DC, Maryland, and Virginia. Insight focuses on business decisions. Homeowner and building energy decisions belong to the separate MBRACE Energy journey. What do I get from the brief builder? + A downloadable worksheet with your four ZIP codes, service focus, chosen question, and a record for collecting observations and sources. It runs in your browser. The optional email link prepares a draft to Max with your scope; you decide whether to send it. How much does a researched brief cost? + The worksheet builder is free to use. This preview does not publish pricing for a researched engagement. Ask Max about scope, fee, and timing before agreeing to any work. Using the builder creates no purchase or subscription. Are these live leads or guaranteed results? + This preview provides no live lead feed or verified project inventory. The builder does not retrieve search rankings or measure your website. A researched brief does not guarantee rankings, calls, revenue, or awarded projects. Where does commercial work fit? + Commercial readiness is a separate qualification question. A public building record can start research; current authority, project need, scope, timing, capacity, and permission still need confirmation before a contractor introduction.
